scope: End-to-end application performance as served by llama-server (HTTP latency, throughput, accuracy). Not a measure of architecture efficiency: the two endpoints build different prompts and do different server-side work; see mean_prompt_tokens and timings.

version: built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
llama_server.n_gpu_layers: all (full offload verified from the load log on every start)

settings.qwen_prediction: harness/models.py rule: argmax of first-token top_logprobs mass over valid answer tokens; normalized text parse used only when logprobs are absent, and reported separately
settings.constrained_decoding: none (no grammar or logit_bias), to keep the CPU harness request unchanged
settings.warmup: 5 requests per server start at the run's concurrency, not measured
settings.throughput: successful HTTP requests / real elapsed wall-clock of the batch (time.perf_counter)
settings.decisions_per_s: throughput_requests_per_s * k (k = questions per request; 1 for spam/routing)
settings.end_to_end_accuracy: correct / all requests (http errors, malformed and unparsed count as wrong)

notes: Prompts and question objects are copied from harness/tasks.py and harness/multiq.py.
Routing criteria use SUBSCRIPTION, not NEWSLETTER.
Concurrency 1 runs on a server started with -np 1; concurrency 4 on a fresh server with -np 4.
The multi-question test uses a seeded random sample of routing items (the CPU harness uses the first 30).
multiq runs each k as its own timed batch (k order shuffled with the same seed).
rep 2: Qwen then d1 on 100 items per task, random.Random(44).sample of each rep 1 set (7.3 min elapsed before rep 2).
